Coarsen a raster or dataset by block means.

coarsen.Rd

Maps x onto the grid factor times coarser, anchored on its origin: each coarse cell is the mean of the valid (non-NaN) values of its factor x factor block, NaN when none is valid. This is exact block arithmetic, not a GDAL resampler, so the two stages stay explicit: a decoded embedding read by nearest neighbour onto a 10 m grid, then averaged to 30 m,

Usage

coarsen(x, factor, fun = "mean")

Arguments

x

A LazyRaster or LazyDataset reading its sources.

factor

Integer block size (>= 1).

fun

Block statistic; only "mean".

Value

A LazyRaster or LazyDataset on the coarser grid (f32).

Details

codes <- lazy_dataset(tiles, grid10, resampling = "near", decode = dequantize_aef)
cube <- stack_bands(coarsen(codes, 3L))

takes, for each 30 m cell, the mean of the nine decoded 10 m values the 10 m read gives, never a GDAL average over the reprojected source footprint. The coarsening runs inside the read: each window's finer cells are assembled from the sources as the nearest-neighbour read of them assembles them (a direct window read of a source on those cells' pixels, a nearest warp of any other source alone, later sources winning where they hold data), decoded, and averaged in one pass, so the finer grid is never written. Cells warped from a reprojected source match the finer read's under garry.warp_exact = TRUE; with GDAL's approximate transformer (the default) a cell near a pixel boundary can take the neighbouring pixel.

Version 1 coarsens reads only: x must come straight from lazy_dataset() or lazy_source() (decoded or not) by nearest-neighbour, from sources opened without open options, and its dims must divide by factor. A dataset with a mask_asset is refused: averaging a mask band's bits would invent flags.
